title: AQ knowledge fixture manifest (v1)
description: The single manifest shape the provider-neutral offline fixture runner (scripts/evaluate-knowledge.py) consumes.  One file per fixture scenario; golden fixtures live in the same directory as this schema.  A manifest pins identities, budget, expected selection, expected omissions, delivery rules and the leakage oracle so a deterministic runner can reproduce the same report on every adapter without a network/provider call.

fixture_id.description: Globally unique, stable identity of this fixture.  Case-sensitive lowercase.

scenario.description: One of the scenario rows from plan section 13, or a named extension.  A synthetic fixture may test semantics; it does not satisfy a later real-incident quality gate by itself.

synthetic.description: True: this fixture is synthetic (or an authorized sanitized reproduction of a real incident).  False is refused by the runner, because the plan says real-incident quality gates are a later explicitly budgeted operation.

source_class.description: synthetic: invented for the fixture. authorized_sanitized: a sanitized reproduction of an operator-authorized incident; still labelled synthetic because the original is not possessed or certified by this runner.

input_hashes.description: SHA-256 of every top-level manifest section the fixture depends on.  Keys 'records', 'expected', 'labels' and 'delivery_rules' are REQUIRED and must each equal the SHA-256 hex of the canonical JSON (sorted keys, compact separators, ASCII) of that section.  Additional keys are allowed for external references (e.g. 'harness_adapter_label') whose name must be in this map.  A mismatched hash is a runner failure.

kind.description: Label the record kind.  Adapters must not re-label without the fixture declaring a kind change.

excerpts.description: Named excerpt bodies keyed by an excerpt label.  The selector reads exactly one excerpt per identity (the one it picks); other labels are allowed for the fixture to express multiple candidate texts.

allowed_identities.description: Identities (record_id + @ + revision_id + : + kind) that the golden selection MUST select, in the canonical order the fixture expects.

omitted_reasons.description: For each identity that MUST be omitted, the exact omission_reason string the runner is expected to record: 'forbidden-identity', 'retired', 'not-current-eligible', 'budget-exceeded', 'context.required_over_budget', 'stale-claim'.

required_budget_diagnostic.description: True when the fixture is the 'required content alone exceeds budget' scenario and the runner MUST emit the context.required_over_budget diagnostic.

forbidden_records.description: Every forbidden identity with the strings the leakage oracle must NOT find in the rendered bundle.  A finding is a runner failure.

provider_labels_allowed.description: Provider/harness labels the rendered bundle is allowed to contain (e.g. ['worker'] — a role label, not a provider).  Empty or absent means no provider label (claude/codex/gemini/opencode/gpt/llama/mistral/deepseek) may appear.

prepared_at.description: Frozen ISO-8601 timestamp the bundle claims; the runner is forbidden from using datetime.now().

role.description: Fixture-level role label.  A golden fixture may specify one role per bundle; cross-role parity is tested by two manifests with different roles but the same expected selection.

harnesses.description: The harness identities this fixture is expected to be valid for.  A cross-adapter fixture includes all of them.  A harness-specific fixture (e.g. 'no-hook') lists one.

adapters.description: The adapter identities the selection is expected to be parity-checked across.  Empty = no adapter parity assertion; non-empty = runner asserts cross-adapter parity on these labels.

role.description: The role this fixture asserts; required when the expected section references role-scoped selection.  Optional for fixtures that do not depend on role.

budget.description: Fixture-level budget.  Defaults when absent: 4096 tokens / 16384 bytes UTF-8 upper bound, no reserved allowance (plan section 9: the 4096-token/16384-byte total knowledge allowance is the discovery default).

expected_forbidden_identity.description: The identity this claim previously held, which MUST NOT be selectable at the current claim_epoch.

stale_claim.description: Stale-revision scenario: a claim from an earlier epoch must be rejected; its prior identity is forbidden for this bundle.  Optional.
